page: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.2xlarge is a general purpose instance designed for workloads with fluctuating compute utilization. Running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8488C processor clocked at 3.2 GHz. It is provisioned with 8 vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores via symmetric multithreading, alongside 105 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 32 GB of high-frequency DDR5 clocked at 5 GHz, providing 4 GB per virtual core. Local storage is not included, requiring external block storage for persistent data, and the instance provides a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong single-threaded throughput, registering top-quartile scores in single-core Geekbench and single-threaded gzip compression. The processor incorporates modern instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which accelerate integer matrix multiplication and floating-point computations. In broader parallel benchmarks, such as multi-core stress-ng tests, Clang compilation, and ray tracing, the instance exhibits mid-range throughput commensurate with its 4-core physical configuration. Memory bandwidth measures 51.52 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 49.46 GB/sec for writes, supporting data-intensive processing within its burstable compute envelope.

The burstable CPU model optimizes cost efficiency for workloads that do not continuously saturate physical execution units. While the instance handles bursty demands effectively, workloads requiring continuous full-capacity multi-core compute, such as intensive 7B parameter LLM text generation where throughput drops to 7.62 tokens per second, experience architectural constraints. The absence of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU accelerators further defines its design boundaries. Consequently, the m7i-flex.2xlarge is best suited for general purpose production services with variable traffic, including web servers, application backends, Redis caching deployments, and software build pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.2xlarge is a burstable general purpose virtual instance based on the AWS Nitro system. It features an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz, providing 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Memory comprises 32 GB of DDR5 operating at 5 GHz, maintaining a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. The instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated graphics hardware, relying on external network-attached storage, with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Computational benchmarks highlight strong single-core performance, evidenced by top-quartile results in Geekbench single-core execution and gzip compression, aided by Intel AMX and AVX-512 vector extensions. However, sustained multi-core tasks and large language model generation settle into average or lower percentiles due to burstable CPU provisioning. This instance is technically matched for variable enterprise workloads, including web servers, application tiers, test environments, and moderate-throughput caching services.
